source_citation: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction, Annex on Chemicals, Schedule 3. Text as published by the OPCW, accessed 2026-08-15.
known_limitations: SCHEDULE 3 LISTING IS NOT A PROHIBITION. These chemicals are listed so that production above certain quantities is declared and may be verified. Every one of them is an ordinary large-scale industrial chemical, and several are among the most common reagents in synthetic chemistry.

The Convention's declaration obligations turn on quantity and concentration. A structure carries neither, so this screen can say that a chemical is listed and can never say whether any obligation applies to anybody.

Schedule 3 entries carry no 'and corresponding salts' wording, unlike several entries in Schedules 1 and 2. This screen strips counter-ions before comparing, so a salt of a listed chemical is reported as a match. That is broader than these entries' own text, and is reported here rather than silently applied.

Entry 11, diethyl phosphite, is NOT ENCODED. Neither structure resolver returns the neutral substance the entry lists: PubChem's record for CAS 762-04-9 is a cation (C4H10O3P+) and OPSIN returns an anion (C4H10O3P-), where diethyl phosphite is the neutral H-phosphonate C4H11O3P. A structure typed by hand would not be traceable to the statute, so the entry is left unresolved and visible rather than guessed.
Mixtures are not considered. A match is on the listed chemical itself.

Every encoded entry is confidence 'verified' rather than 'exact': each names a substance whose identity was checked against the CAS printed in the entry. 'exact' is reserved for a rule transcribing a structural specification the regulation itself gives, which Schedule 3 never does.
